episode.tagline: Complex AI. Explained visually. Built practically.
episode.title: What Is MCP, and Why Does It Matter?
episode.disclosure: Fictional teaching scenario. Wouri Express and its people are invented; the setting draws on documented conditions in Douala, Cameroon. MCP facts: the Model Context Protocol is an open standard published by Anthropic in November 2024.

onScreen.text: Three systems. Two AI models. Six custom connections to maintain.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Wouri Express has three systems: the delivery sheet, the driver messages, and a map service. And two AI models that need them.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: That is six custom connections to build and maintain. The Model Context Protocol, MCP, turns six into three. Here is how.

onScreen.title: What Is MCP, and Why Does It Matter?
onScreen.subtitle: AI Fundamentals · Lesson 8 · One connector per system at Wouri Express, Douala

messages.text: Ndedi: The sheet changed one column and the Delay Analyst broke. Then the risk model broke too. Same column.
Ndedi: Every model has its own way of reading my sheet. I fix the same thing twice.

ui.title: Mbella's rule
lines: I want to switch AI providers without rebuilding everything
And I want to see exactly what each model is allowed to touch

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: One column changed, Tanyi, and both AI systems broke. Ndedi fixed the same thing twice, once for each model.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Mbella wants to switch providers without rebuilding, and to see what each model may touch. Both are what MCP is for.

scenes.label: Decide: custom code or a standard

left.title: Custom integrations
items: One connection per model, per system

right.title: MCP
items: One server per system, any model connects
Tools and permissions listed in one place

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Custom integrations mean one connection per model, per system. Each breaks on its own, and permissions hide inside the code.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: MCP is an open standard. You build one MCP server per system, and any model that speaks the protocol can connect.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: A standard connector is not a safe connector. The server decides which tools exist. That is where I look first.

onScreen.title: Models, MCP servers, and the company's systems

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: On the left, the models. On the right, the company's systems. In the middle, one MCP server per system.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Each server publishes a short list of tools. Read a week. Export messages, already stripped. Measure a distance. Nothing else exists.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Any model connects the same way. Change the sheet, fix one server. Change the model, the servers stay. That is why it matters.

items.text: read_week(week): deliveries and delays for one week
read_delivery(id): one delivery, no customer phone
That is all. No write, no delete

steps.title: Connect a model
steps.detail: The model asks what tools exist

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: The sheet server has two tools. Read a week. Read one delivery, without the customer's phone. No write, no delete.

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: So the model asks the server what it can do, then calls a tool by name. It never touches the sheet directly.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: When Mbella tries a second provider, the same server answers the same way. No code changed.

ui.title: Review
lines: delete_week: one wrong call erases a week
send_customer_sms: the never list says no

lines.speaker: hallucinator
lines.text: Why stop at reading? Give the server update, delete and send SMS. One connector, unlimited power. Efficient.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Every tool is a permission. Delete week erases a week with one wrong call. Send SMS breaks the never list. I keep read only.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: MCP makes connecting easy. That is exactly why you list tools carefully. Read tools for the agent. Write tools behind a person's click.

messages.text: Ndedi: I renamed the “late” column to “delayed”.
Sheet server updated once. Delay Analyst and risk explainer both read week 39 correctly.

steps.title: A write goes through a person

ui.title: Apply proposed update: delivery 88 cause = road?
summary: Proposed by the Delay Analyst via sheet-write

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Ndedi renames a column. I update the sheet server once, and both models read week thirty-nine correctly.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: When the analyst wants to correct the sheet, it proposes. Ndedi applies. MCP carries the request. She holds the pen.

items.label: Any office
items.text: A documents server: search and read, never delete

items.label: Clinic
items.text: An appointments server: read slots, propose bookings

items.label: Accounting
items.text: An invoices server: read and flag, payments stay human

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: One server per system, anywhere: documents to search but never delete, appointments to read and propose, invoices to flag while payments stay human.

onScreen.title: Who owns this?
items: Wouri Express owns its MCP servers and their tool lists
The provider can change; the servers stay
Every tool call is logged with the model that made it

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: The company owns its servers and their tool lists. The provider can change; the servers stay. Every call is logged. Whoever approves a write is accountable.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: MCP: an open standard so any model reaches your systems through one connector each. It matters because the tool list, and the power, stay in your hands.

onScreen.title: Your build challenge
items: List the three systems your AI would need
For each, write the read tools
Then the write tools that need a click

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Your challenge: list the three systems your AI would need. For each, write the read tools, then the write tools that need a click.

kito.name: Kito
kito.role: Small AI assistant who demonstrates concepts and occasionally makes believable mistakes.

hallucinator.role: Mischievous. Represents confident but incorrect AI output.

gatekeeper.role: Represents security, privacy, governance and human approval.
